title: Per-token Dequant Credit Allocator & Kernel Hedging for Mixed-Precision Prefill
creator: Ava Mitchell
description:
Problem: dequant overhead is a measurable source of latency jitter during streaming decode and prefill, especially on mixed-precision pipelines that interleave INT8 and FP8 kernels. Current kernel selection favors static cost heuristics and often triggers expensive dequant/requant transitions at token boundaries, amplifying tail latency for medium-length inputs.

Goal: implement a per-token dequant credit allocator and kernel hedging strategy that: (1) tracks amortized dequant cost per request, (2) allows the scheduler to borrow/repay "dequant credits" to postpone or advance dequant transitions, and (3) integrates with the kernel selector to bias toward cheaper kernel fragments when credit budget is low. The end goal is to reduce 95th/99th latency for prefill and early decode windows without regressing average throughput or quality.

Scope: runtime + kernel selector + prefill scheduler + telemetry. This ticket covers design, prototype implementation on the Linux CUDA runtime path (A100 & H100), integration tests, microbenching, and a canary rollout for dedicated customers.
acceptance_criteria: 95th-percentile prefill latency reduced by >= 18% on mixed-precision workloads compared to baseline
No more than 2% throughput regression (tokens/sec) on steady-state streaming decode when credits are active
Kernel selector exposes a bounded API for token-credit hints and hedging flags
End-to-end integration tests for correctness across INT8/FP8 transitions with KV cache preserved
Production canary rollout procedure documented and rollback tested
tasks: Design dequant credit accounting model and API for kernel selector
Add telemetry counters for per-token dequant cost and credit balance (sampling + full traces)
Implement allocator (lock-free per-request shard) and integrate with prefill scheduler
Expose hedging hint in kernel selection path: prefer partial-precision microkernels under low-credit state
Write unit/integration tests that validate KV cache invariants across dequant transitions
Run microbench matrix (batch sizes, seq lengths, head dims) on A100/H100 and collect 50k sample latencies
Prepare canary rollout dashboard and rollback playbook
notes: Trade-offs considered: conservative credit accumulation avoids hallucination of cost savings but may underutilize opportunities for latency reduction; aggressive hedging reduces tail but can increase token cost due to extra kernel invocations.
We will initially restrict hedging to attention and softmax-adjacent kernels where dequant cost is empirically highest; matmul/memory-bound kernels are out-of-scope for the first pass.
The allocator will operate in 'token ticks' where each token contributes a sampled cost delta; a low-overhead EWMA estimator chosen to limit telemetry noise.
Fallback: if the allocator indicates inconsistent telemetry (missing samples > 10%), revert to current static kernel cost heuristic to avoid oscillation.
benchmark_summary: Baseline microbench (mixed INT8/FP8, batch=1, seq=128) median=22.3ms, p95=48.8ms, p99=82.1ms
Prototype with naive crediter (no hedging) reduced p95 by 9% but regressed median by 1.4%
Current design target expects p95 improvements of 18-25% with <2% median throughput regression after tuning
implementation_notes: Allocator data-structure: per-request 64-bit counters sharded by worker thread; updates via relaxed atomics to avoid stalls
Kernel selector contract: add hint enum {FORCE_FP, FORCE_INT, HEDGE_PREFER_INT_PART, NO_HINT} and an integer credit_budget parameter
Prefill scheduler changes: allow speculative postpone of dequant transition for up to N tokens if credit_budget > threshold; otherwise schedule immediate transition
Quality guardrails: compare outputs on a sampled 0.1% of requests to validate no regression in token distribution (BLEU/ROUGE style on synthetic prompts)
Config knobs: credit accumulation rate, hedging max length, EWMA alpha, sampling fraction — all exposed via remote config for fast tuning
